artifacts.summary: T1/T1' machine-verified sorry-free in a compiled spike; T2 is a ~650-line label-only transposition of BiLasso/Decide.lean; T3's negative #guard is infeasible by ~12 orders of magnitude and needs a scope decision.

262-line compiled spike: WitnessFamily.std ShiftSet, the agreement induction through ShiftSet.forward_repr, and the three consequence corollaries; zero sorry, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

user_decision.question: T3's second deliverable -- a #guard that no witness family with all segment lengths <= 2 exists for the negation of MF -- is computationally infeasible: subformulaClosure(MF.neg) has card 10, so up to 1024^6 (~1.2e18) label assignments must be enumerated for a single lasso. Which substitute should the plan carry?
options: Prove a theorem no_witnessFamily_of_MF_neg directly (BoxFaithful makes bx a global constant, so MF.neg's two box clauses are contradictory at any single family) -- recommended
Hand-build a rejected family and #guard !decide (...), mirroring BiLasso/Examples.lean's negAnnot -- recommended alongside option 1
Keep the enumeration but shrink to segment lengths exactly (1,0,1) over a hand-picked 2-formula sub-closure (smoke test only)
Keep the acceptance criterion as written and accept that the #guard will not terminate
user_decision.recommendation: Options 1 and 2 together. They deliver the content T3 was reaching for -- a real impossibility result plus genuine predicate separation -- at no enumeration cost.
